description:
UNVERIFIED - A/B ONLY, DO NOT SHIP BLIND. This is a c-INFERRED lever and it is filed under the repo's UNVERIFIED-AB convention deliberately. Apply it ON ITS OWN, play ONE match, and look at it. If you cannot tell the difference, revert it and forget it - that is the most likely outcome and it costs you nothing.

WHY IT IS HERE AT ALL. It is mechanically trivial and reverts in seconds, and if the inference is right it widens the class of contacts that play the bigger, more side-on stagger, which is squarely what you asked for. But this project has been confidently wrong from static inference before - a spin axis, an 'error is exactly zero' claim, an assist-flag theory and a duel byte that did the opposite of its description - and this claim has exactly that shape. So it is not in the shipping set.

WHAT CHANGES. match::anime::action::Stagger::vf30 (0x143effd70) contains a comparison at 0x143f00081 against 45.0. If the value in xmm6 exceeds 45, a branch is taken that sets motion id 0x226 or 0x221 (at 0x143f0008f and 0x143f000a2); if not, execution falls through to a second branch at 0x143f000b5 which tests 78.75. This pack lowers the 45 to 30 by re-aiming the comparison's disp32 to an existing pool cell. No shared cell is written.

WHAT IS CERTAIN (b-DISASSEMBLY). The instruction at 0x143f00081 is 'comiss xmm6, [rip+disp32]', the cell it reads holds 45.0, the following 'jbe 0x143f000b5' skips the branch, and that branch does set motion ids 0x226 and 0x221. The site is byte-identical between the INSTALLED image and eFootball.exe.PRISTINE (both 0F2F3588D8C101) and the re-aimed disp32 was recomputed by hand this pass as 0x145a8dd80 - 0x143f00088 = 0x1b8dcf8, with the target cell confirmed to hold 30.0.

WHAT IS INFERRED AND NOT PROVEN (c-INFERRED). Two things, and the second is the one that matters. (1) That xmm6 is an approach angle in degrees - it is produced by 0x143c88e20 at 0x143f0000b applied to two direction vectors, which is suggestive but was not emulated. (2) THAT THE 45-DEGREE BRANCH IS VISUALLY 'STRONGER' OR MORE DRAMATIC THAN THE FALL-THROUGH BRANCH AT 0x143f000b5, WHICH WAS NEVER DECODED. If that is backwards, this pack makes staggers look TAMER, not heavier. Nobody has established which way round it is. This is the entire reason the pack is quarantined.

WHO IT AFFECTS: everyone, if it does anything - your stick-controlled player, your AI team-mates and the CPU.

IT DOES NOT CHANGE HOW OFTEN ANYONE FALLS. Like falls-ballhit-severity, this selects an animation inside a stagger that has already been decided on.

EXPECTED EFFECT ON FOULS AND CARDS: NONE. Animation selection only; no score term and no whistle or card threshold is touched.

WHAT TO LOOK FOR IN ONE MATCH. Whether staggers from angled contact look bigger and more side-on, or smaller and more clipped. Either answer is useful - write down which one you saw. Do not run this together with any other pack or you will not be able to attribute what you see.

WHAT WOULD MEAN IT IS TOO STRONG - OR SIMPLY WRONG. Staggers looking flatter and less dramatic than stock means the inference is backwards and the pack should be discarded. Staggers looking exaggerated on glancing, near-head-on contact means it is too strong. No visible difference means the angle theory is wrong; discard.

COLLISIONS: none. Not in the applied kick-error bytes (0x14401b423, 0x14401a12c, 0x1440187b4, 0x14105ed1e) and not overlapping any unapplied spec. It DOES sit in the same function as falls-ballhit-severity.json (Stagger::vf30) but at a different instruction - do not apply both at once, for attribution reasons rather than safety.

REVERT: python tools/exe_patch.py remove tools/data/patches/falls-stagger-angle-UNVERIFIED-AB.json

patches.name: stagger motion-branch angle gate 45 -> 30 degrees (disp32 re-aim) - UNVERIFIED
patches.note: comiss xmm6,[rip+0x1c1d888 -> 0x145b1d910 = 45.0] re-aimed to [rip+0x1b8dcf8 -> 0x145a8dd80 = 30.0]. disp32 recomputed by hand as 0x145a8dd80 - 0x143f00088 = 0x1b8dcf8. Both cells confirmed to hold 45.0 and 30.0 in the installed image. No pool cell is written. The DIRECTION of the visual effect is NOT established - see the description.
